native_retrieval.title: India’s Cockroach protests: Rahul Gandhi detained after calling for PM Modi to resign - The Guardian
native_retrieval.snippet: Opposition leader taken away after accusing Narendra Modi of ‘destroying the future of India’s youth’ during protest in solidarity with cockroach movement. Indian police briefly detained opposition leader Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday during protests calling for prime minister Narendra Modi’s resignation, in solidarity with the new youth-led cockroach party movement. Gandhi, the leader of India’s Congress party, staged a sit-in outside Modi’s house on Tuesday afternoon, stating that Modi must resign “for destroying the future of India’s youth”. His protest took place as thousands of students were gathered at a separate site in central Delhi, the day after a huge protest calling for the resignation of Modi’s education minister was met with brutality by Delhi police, including baton attacks and teargas. Gandhi said his party was taking their protest directly to the prime minister’s house, after the Modi government refused to take up the issues of the students and the alleged “brutality unleashed on students” in parliament.

native_retrieval.title: How India's youth-led 'Cockroach' movement challenges Modi - DW.com
native_retrieval.snippet: # How India's youth-led 'Cockroach' movement challenges Modi. What started as a satirical protest against exam leaks in India has grown into a wider movement voicing young Indians' anger over jobs and education. Riot police fired tear gas and used batons in New Delhi as tens of thousands of supporters of the satirical Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) marched towards India's Parliament on Monday (July 20). The CJP began as an online campaign in May and rapidly evolved into a Gen Z street movement, giving a voice to a generation frustrated by unemployment, shrinking opportunities and a failing education system. The youth-led "Cockroach" party is now posing an unexpected challenge for Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government, prompting a response that combines political outreach with police action. This is a worthless government," Renuka Chowdhury, an MP from India's opposition Congress party, told DW. The CJP movement gained fresh momentum over the weekend after veteran reform activist Sonam Wangchuk, whose three-week hunger strike has become a symbol of the protests, was forcibly taken to a hospital by police.

native_retrieval.title: India’s youth-led Cockroach movement vows to keep demanding reforms after police crackdown - Greenwich Time
native_retrieval.snippet: # India’s youth-led Cockroach movement vows to keep demanding reforms after police crackdown. NEW DELHI (AP) — Supporters of India’s youth-led Cockroach movement demanding educational reforms and government accountability refused to leave their New Delhi protest site Tuesday, a day after their thousands-strong march toward Parliament drew police tear gas, beatings and a new wave of sympathy from across the country. The movement, now attracting professionals and families beyond students, represents a rare public challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s government, reviving criticism over its handling of dissent and use of force to respond to protests. Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and dozens of his Congress party lawmakers showed their support Tuesday with a sit-in outside Modi’s residence before police forcibly removed them in a dramatic escalation. Government minister Jitendra Singh said Gandhi was told the location was not “suitable for a sit-in.". Ada's coffee and candy shop on course to reopen in Riverside part of Greenwich.
